findings.title: Continue starts a new run
findings.evidence: CLOSED in 8dd3469/7f7162f/5ea09eb: explicit RunLaunchRequest (NEW_RUN/CONTINUE), the Continue path calls resume_run(), a failed Continue creates no replacement run and never overwrites the save. Suite: tests/run_integrity/continue_routing_test.gd (16/0).

findings.title: save DTO does not represent the actual checkpoint
findings.evidence: CLOSED in 952b0e5: core/save/save_schema_v5.gd is the canonical checkpoint schema. The v4 hardcodes (phase=prep, shop/map/rewards={}) are gone; the wire phase is prep/map/reward/merchant. Suite: tests/run_integrity/checkpoint_roundtrip_test.gd (41/0).

findings.title: resume reconstructs random state instead of restoring it
findings.evidence: CLOSED in bf2a157 + 03e7992: the subsystems have exact snapshot/restore (EncounterMap, Shop, ShopScreen merchant, RewardScreen), the resume restores instead of regenerating, and the v5 load path applies the semantic gate. Suite: tests/run_integrity/subsystem_snapshot_test.gd (37/0), checkpoint_roundtrip_test.gd (41/0).

findings.title: RNG continuation is not persisted
findings.evidence: CLOSED in 952b0e5 + 3752907 + 48a08d8: rng.state is persisted as a lossless decimal string (the machine state is NOT an IEEE-754 safe integer) and the machine state is ALWAYS restored, before the live commit. Suite: tests/run_integrity/rng_wire_precision_test.gd (64/0), rng_resume_continuity_test.gd (10/0).

findings.title: battle result is saved before it is applied
findings.evidence: CLOSED in f525693 + dfa26d6 + 1b4c58a + 5a804ac. The outcome of a finished battle is now ONE transaction: the outcome is applied first and written after it, in a single write that carries the reward offer, the shop offer and the stream position. The loss branch writes too, after the shop refresh. A finished run removes its file, so it can never be resumed past MAX_ROUND. The idempotence is a one-shot latch in the controller, so even a reset of the runner phase cannot re-apply the outcome. Suite: tests/run_integrity/battle_outcome_transaction_test.gd (9 cases). Negative controls NC-18..NC-24 are honest REDs.

findings.title: pending reward is not actually persisted
findings.evidence: CLOSED in 952b0e5: the reward offer is part of the v5 checkpoint (offered ids + order + round index) and is restored, not regenerated. Suite: tests/run_integrity/checkpoint_roundtrip_test.gd (41/0).

findings.title: new run may retain old runtime objects
findings.evidence: core/progression/run_controller.gd:76-105 start_run() creates a fresh state and calls _refresh_shop(), but never resets encounter_map, reward, runner, ctx, _battle_participants or the phase-dependent flags. The only battle entry point in core/ is start_battle() (run_controller.gd:473).

findings.title: final boss termination depends only on battle count
findings.evidence: core/progression/run_controller.gd:628 and :909 terminate the run only on state.round_index > BalanceScript.MAX_ROUND. core/encounter/encounter_map.gd:45-46 and :99-106 build an explicit BOSS node on depth 10, but the boss node does not drive the run completion.

findings.title: command/domain guards are incomplete
findings.evidence: CLOSED in ed71b8c + 3eccaa2. The guards are DERIVED from one table (RunController.COMMAND_PHASES), the machine-readable form of docs/ri09_command_phase_matrix.md, so they cannot become a scatter of ad-hoc conditions that drift apart. A refusal is logged and changes NOTHING: the guard is the FIRST statement of the command, so no gold, no inventory, no unit, no map/reward state, no RNG draw, no event and no checkpoint can be touched. A command that is not in the table is refused too. The matrix was corrected against the CODE before it was implemented: the inventory is an overlay inside the battle scene and is reachable in every phase, and the equipment bonuses are read once at the start of a battle, so the equipment commands are allowed in every live phase -- a naive PREP-only guard would have broken the inventory UI. Suite: tests/run_integrity/command_phase_guard_test.gd (5 cases). Negative controls NC-28..NC-31 are honest REDs.

findings.title: bench capacity / purchase atomicity
findings.evidence: core/progression/run_controller.gd:109-126 buy_unit() checks phase, offer and gold, then mutates gold (:119), creates the unit (:121) and takes the offer (:122) - it never checks the bench capacity. core/balance.gd:83 MAX_BENCH_UNITS = 4 exists but is not consulted here.

findings.title: no run-integrity test suite exists
findings.evidence: tests/ has no run_integrity/ directory. The existing suites cover the v4 mapper and the save repository, but none of them asserts a checkpoint round trip, RNG continuation, battle outcome transaction or phase guard.

findings.title: schema v5 does not exist
findings.evidence: CLOSED in 952b0e5: core/save/save_schema_v5.gd is the canonical checkpoint-capable schema, with a pure mapper (core/progression/run_checkpoint_v5_mapper.gd) and the v4->v5 migration path. Suite: tests/run_integrity/v4_migration_test.gd (9/0), checkpoint_determinism_test.gd (9/0).

notes: All twelve source-confirmed findings were re-audited on the actual HEAD dcab44e. Every one of them is still present. The battle backend, the save repository hardening and the battle content are NOT touched by this gauntlet.

critic_rounds.findings: H-1 (a v4 save taken after the map was entered could never be continued), m-1 (the encounter-map overlay reseeded the global run RNG), m-2 (the v5 load path had no semantic validation)

HIGH-1 (the extracted validator was weaker than the original v4 gate: the bidirectional equipment consistency was missing), HIGH-2 (the v5 load path CRASHED on a shape-invalid file: a Dictionary was passed to add_diagnostic), MINOR-1 (the seed-0 guard skipped the stream restore), MINOR-2 (the v4 migration did not state the map fallback consequence)

M-1 (the v5 canonical LOAD path did not run the semantic gate), M-2 (the v5 SAVE path applied only validate_shape, so the real gate fired after the commit and a fresh slot kept the invalid file), MINOR-1 (the sequence cursor rule rejected a legal live state after a removal), MINOR-2 (the RNG restore happened after the live commit), MINOR-3 (the mapper accepted a lossy numeric rng state)

M1 (the win path was two writes, so the reward offer was lost on a crash between them), M2 (the continuing-loss checkpoint was written before the shop refresh, so it carried a stale shop offer and a stale RNG position), M3 (the game-over path left a resumable 'prep' checkpoint at a finished round), m1..m7 (the magic phase numbers in the runner, the APPLIED doc comment, the state-based idempotence guard, the participant-bridge rationale, the test coverage, the write-failure behaviour)

H1 (the MAX_ROUND win wrote a resumable checkpoint and removed it afterwards, so a crash in the window resurrected a finished run past MAX_ROUND), M1 (delete_run left the .commit-old behind and the recovery path resurrected the deleted slot), M2 (the delete result was discarded, so a failed removal was silent), M3 (the idempotence latch was consumed before the write, so a failed write stranded the outcome with no retry), m1 (get_save_count counts attempts, not successful writes), m2 (a dead reward offer at MAX_ROUND), m3 (resume_run bypassed the meta seam)

no critic: the thirteen unguarded commands were already confirmed in the ledger, and the matrix was derived from the CODE rather than from the finding, which corrected the ledger: the equipment commands are legal in every live phase because the inventory overlay is reachable at any time and the equipment bonuses are read once, at the start of a battle

cursor_contract.decision: the project owner chose the monotonic-cursor rule
cursor_contract.reason: the allocator never reuses or wraps a consumed id and a removal does not roll the cursor back, so a gap is normal and valid; tombstones are NOT introduced

ci_defect_found_after_the_first_push.summary: the isolation seam broke the READ path: the suites wrote through the injected repository but read through the production SaveService, so the read found nothing
ci_defect_found_after_the_first_push.why_the_local_gate_missed_it: the local box kept the files of the earlier runs in user://, so the production read found a stale file; the CI box is always clean
ci_defect_found_after_the_first_push.fix: the read uses the same repository as the write, through the SaveService._load_run_v4_with_repository seam; every suite now has its OWN isolated directory
ci_defect_found_after_the_first_push.lesson: a gate that runs against a dirty state is weaker than the CI. The clean-state run is the honest one, and it must be the default: the suites now clean their own directory.
